intro: Provence is still being built out along Hamilton Pool Road, with homes from Ashton Woods, David Weekley, Westin, Newmark, Drees and Toll. CleanzATX cleans new construction windows and keeps them clear after move in.

paragraphs: Provence is the newest community in the Bee Cave area, and it is still growing. Several builders are active at once, including Ashton Woods, David Weekley, Westin, Newmark, Drees and Toll, so a single street can show several floor plans. Homes run from 2,200 to 5,500 square feet, with prices from the mid $500Ks up to about $1.5M. The design leans European, with stucco, stone accents and arched details, and there is a pool and clubhouse for residents. There is no gate, but there is a Provence HOA and a MUD, so ask your management company if exterior work has any posted guidelines.
Many homes here are brand new or only a year or two old.

New construction glass has its own problems. Labels, stucco overspray, paint flecks and a gray film of drywall and saw dust are common right after closing, and ordinary spray cleaners smear it around. With nearby lots still being graded and framed, dust drifts over finished homes all day. Young yards mean sprinklers set high, and our hard water leaves white spots on lower windows within a few months. Trees are small, so the sun reaches the glass directly, and west facing panes show every smear.
The upside is that new glass is in good shape, so a careful first cleaning with pure water, and a scrape of anything stubborn, sets it up to stay easy.

With no gate, we show up and start. Water fed poles reach up to three stories from the ground, so we can clean stucco homes without ladders against fresh paint. Inside, we use drop cloths and hand squeegees and take care around new flooring. Because Provence keeps growing, we route several homes on the same street when neighbors book together, and that helps with scheduling. A first clean after move in often includes screens and tracks, which collect builder dust. Stucco is soft washed only at low pressure, and new concrete flatwork is cleaned at $0.18 per square foot.
A 2,800 square foot home is about $280 for exterior windows, so the $200 minimum job is not a factor. Expect roughly two to three hours outside and about an hour and a half inside.

faq.q: Can you clean windows right after I move into a new build?
faq.a: Yes. We remove label residue, light paint flecks and construction film with pure water and careful scraping. Stubborn stucco overspray or heavy paint may need a separate approach, and we tell you before we start.

faq.q: Will cleaning damage my new windows?
faq.a: No. We use soft tools and pure water, never abrasive pads on coated glass. If we see a defect or a deep scratch already there, we point it out first so you know it was not caused by the cleaning.

faq.q: What does a typical Provence home cost?
faq.a: Exterior windows are about $0.10 per square foot, so a 2,800 square foot home is about $280. Cleaning inside and out in Provence is $15 per window. Screens and tracks are $5 each.

faq.q: Do I need to be home?
faq.a: For exterior only, no, as long as we can reach the windows. For interior cleaning someone should be there or have given access. We text before arriving.

faq.q: Are there HOA rules about hiring a cleaner?
faq.a: We are not aware of any that apply to cleaning itself. We recommend checking with your HOA if you plan any work outside the home, such as pressure washing, since parking or noise times may be posted.

faq.q: Do you offer a plan for a new home?
faq.a: Yes. The Clean Windows Club starts at 10% off for Twice a Year. Quarterly and Every 2 Months add a free yearly screen cleaning and the 7 day rain guarantee, which helps in a dusty, growing area.
